2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

On the basis of pleadings of the parties, evidence adduced and arguments addressed,
issue wise findings are as under:
Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 05.09.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicl

12. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2
The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture MACT NO:739/21 Sabir Khan v. Karan Bery P.No. 6 Of 21 BK with reference to the nature of
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could hav

13. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation,
n
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases,
compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv).

13.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii),
(v) and (vi) relating to loss of futu
13.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence.

13.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof.
13.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves d
Decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Courts contain necessary guidelines for award under these heads, if necessary.

13.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder:
"10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a MACT NO:739/21 Sabir Khan v. Karan Bery P.No. 8 Of 21 BK result of the permanent ability (thi
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii)
whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be Sabir Khan (Dar) vs Karan Bery(213/18, Ppp) on 23 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://i

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a conseq

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some o

It may be noted that when compensation is awarded by treating the loss of future earning capacity as 100% (or even anything more than 50%), the need to award compensation separately under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation
As regards loss of income, petitioner has claimed to be working as Office Assistant at TCM(Twenty First Century Media Pvt. Ltd.) and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
Petitioner has filed a salary certificate Ex.PW-1/6, to prove his employment and income.

During his cross-examination, Respondent no.3 disputed the employment and salary as claimed by the petitioner, however, no document or other evidence had been produced by the respondents to counter the certificate Ex.PW-1/6 relied upon by t
There is nothing to doubt that based on the qualification of the petitioner i.e. 10th passed, he could not have been working as Office Assistant or earning Rs.12,000/- p.m.
As such, monthly income of the petitioner stands proved to be Rs.12,000/-.

As per MLC Ex.PW-1/1 and discharge summary of Trauma Center AIIMS Ex.PW-1/2,
petitioner was admitted on 05.09.2018 and discharged on 03.10.2018.
Period of his hospitalization is about one month.
The nature of injury suffered by the petitioner is opined to be grievous in nature and his medical documents reveal that he suffered fracture on right clavical.

In these circumstances, it is expected that the petitioner may have continued to be on bed rest for at least four months(inclusive of period of hospitalization) and incapacitated from working during that period.

Accordingly,
petitioner is entitled to compensation towards loss of income equal to MACT NO:739/21 Sabir Khan v. Karan Bery P.No. 10 Of 21 BK Rs.12,000/-X4=Rs.48,000/-.

He has been diagnosed with physical impairment in Post RTA left hemiparesis.
Petitioner has also claimed to have suffered neurological disorder on account of injury sustained in the accident.
To prove the same, he has relied upon an OPD slip/card Ex.PW-1/11, showing consultation with a Psychiatric at AIIMS.
A careful perusal of this treatment card shows that the patient had complained of memory deficits.
However, there is no final observation or assessment of his neurological problem.
Further, the OPD slip shows the first reference/consultation of the petitioner in the Psychiatric department on 28.05.2024 i.e. after almost three years of the accident.
No nexus or co-relation between the accident and the neurological disorder, if any has been established.
Hence, it cannot be said that the petitioner has suffered neurological disability on account of the injury sustained in the accident.

Considering the nature of employment, educational qualification of the petitioner and the body part in which permanent disability of 65% has been observed, the functional disability of the petitioner is taken to be 30%.
As per record, date of birth of petitioner is 31.08.1998.

Thus, on the date of accident(05.09.2018), he would have been around 20 years of MACT NO:739/21 Sabir Khan v.

As such, for purpose of calculating loss of future income, a multiplier of 18, as per Sarla Verma judgment, would be applicable in the case and 40% would be added as future prospect as Pranay Sethi judgment.

Hence, compensation towards loss of future income is assessed to Rs.12000/-(monthly income)X12(annual computation)X18(multiplier)+40%
of total income(as future prospect)=Rs.36,28,800/-.
30% of this amount would be Rs.10,88,640/-.
Hence so awarded.
